issues.title: SSO configuration screen confusing and sections in wrong order
issues.screen: Admin Manager > Organization > Authentication > SSO tab
issues.summary: The screen shows the paste-back step before the copy-out step, so users hit a dead end before they have anything to enter — with no indication they need to leave and return.

labels: Single Log Off Call Back URL
Add SnapLogic application in your identity provider
Provide SnapLogic metadata to your IdP
problems: Metadata upload section (second-visit task) appears at the top, before the SnapLogic-generated URLs the user needs first
No indication that this is a two-pass workflow requiring the user to leave and return
The page acts as both source (copy values out) and destination (paste metadata back) with no explanation of either role
Users attempt to upload IdP metadata before the IdP app exists, because they cannot yet have the metadata

proposed_fix.approach: Numbered two-step layout that makes the two-pass workflow explicit

steps.heading: Copy SnapLogic values for your identity provider
steps.body: Copy the values below and use them to create a SAML application in your identity provider (Okta, Azure AD, etc.). Then return to this page to complete Step 2.
elements: Download metadata file (alternative for IdPs that accept file format)

steps.heading: Upload your identity provider metadata
steps.subheading: Complete after finishing Step 1 in your identity provider
steps.body: After creating your SAML application in your IdP, export the metadata file and upload it here.
elements: Single Log Off Call Back URL field

issues.interactive_description: Mini mock showing the two-pass flow: Step 1 (copy values) → tooltip or modal saying 'Now go configure your IdP and return' → Step 2 (upload metadata) becomes active

annotations.callout: Users see this first — but they can't complete it yet. The IdP app doesn't exist until they use values from lower on this same page.

annotations.target: Entity ID / Reply URL / Logout URL section
annotations.callout: The values users need first are presented second, with no instruction to copy them and go elsewhere.
This page plays two roles at two different times — source and destination — but nothing on the page communicates that.
